topics: 🌾 New Mishna: A Chain of 'Only According to Calculation' Halakhot
⚖️ Teruma Falls Twice — Rabbi Eliezer vs. the Rabbis on a doubly-mixed batch
💧 Drawn Water and the Ritual Bath — three opinions on how much invalidates it
🌫️ Dust Before Water? — Rabbi Shimon's gezeirah shava for the red heifer's ashes
🔁 A Substitute Doesn't Make Another Substitute — and neither does an offspring (Rabbi Yehuda dissents)

overview.title: 📖 Overview: A Mishna of Non-Propagating Sanctities
overview.subtitle: Temurah 12a–12b
overview.hebrewSource: וְאֵין תְּמוּרָה עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה, וְלֹא הַוָּלָד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: A new mishna groups together a striking list of halakhot that share one structure: a status, once diluted or transferred, does not simply keep propagating at full strength into further mixtures — teruma mixed again only counts proportionally, leavening agent works only if enough survives, drawn water invalidates a ritual bath only by a threshold count, the red heifer's purifying water requires ash placed onto water (not the reverse), and a beit haperas (a plowed grave-field) does not contaminate a second field the same way. The mishna's final and most direct application to our tractate: a substitute animal does not itself generate a further substitute, and the offspring of a consecrated animal does not become a substitute either — a point Rabbi Yehuda disputes. The Gemara identifies which tanna each halakha follows and works through the reasoning behind several of them.

slides.title: 🌾 The Mishna's Chain: Six 'Non-Propagating' Halakhot
slides.subtitle: Each shares the same structure: a status doesn't simply spread at full strength
rows: Teruma mixed, then mixed again elsewhere
Only according to the proportional calculation, not as full teruma
Dough leavened by teruma leaven, remixed
Only leavens the new batch according to calculation
Drawn water (3 log) added to a ritual bath
Invalidates it only per a specific threshold, not automatically
Water of the red heifer (mei chatat)
Becomes purifying water only when ash is placed ONTO water, not water onto ash
Does not create a second beit haperas if plowed further
Does not itself generate another substitute; nor does an animal's offspring

callout.label: Unifying theme:
callout.text: In every case, a derivative or diluted status stops propagating in full force — it does not automatically confer its own status on whatever it later touches.

slides.title: ⚖️ Teruma Falls Into a Mixture, Then Falls Again
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Eliezer vs. the Rabbis on a se'ah taken from an already-mixed batch

lines.speaker: Case
lines.text: A se'ah of teruma falls into fewer than 100 se'ah of non-sacred produce (not nullified). Then a se'ah is taken FROM that mixture and falls into yet more non-sacred produce.

lines.speaker: Rabbi Eliezer
lines.text: That se'ah renders the new batch forbidden as if it were pure teruma — perhaps the original teruma never truly dispersed and came out intact.

lines.speaker: The Rabbis
lines.text: No — it renders the new batch forbidden only according to the calculated proportion of real teruma actually present, assuming even distribution.

lines.speaker: Ruling
lines.text: Our mishna follows the Rabbis, not Rabbi Eliezer — diluted status carries forward only in proportion, not at full strength.

callout.label: Same logic, different context:
callout.text: This is the very principle the mishna later applies to temurah: a derivative status (the substitute) does not carry the same generative power as the original.

slides.title: 💧 How Much Drawn Water Invalidates a Ritual Bath?
slides.subtitle: Three positions reconciled by Rabba

nodes.content: ❓ The mishna says drawn water invalidates a mikveh 'only according to calculation' — what calculation?
🅰️ R' Eliezer ben Yaakov: drawn water is purified by flowing WITH existing valid water — invalid only if drawn water is the majority
🅱️ Difficulty: R' Yoḥanan elsewhere says water that flowed in, even entirely drawn, is pure — matching neither the Rabbis nor R' Eliezer ben Yaakov
✅ Rabba's resolution: the calculation is of VESSELS — Yosef ben Ḥoni: 2-3 vessels of drawn water invalidate it, but spread across 4-5 vessels, it does not

callout.label: Point:
callout.text: Even a small technical detail — how many vessels poured the water — determines whether the 'calculation' rule protects the mikveh's validity.

slides.title: 🌫️ Must the Water Go Into the Vessel First?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Shimon derives a gezeirah shava between the red heifer and the sota

lines.speaker: Mishna
lines.text: If one places the ashes into the vessel before the water, the mixture is unfit for the red heifer's purification.

lines.speaker: Rabbi Shimon
lines.text: I deem it fit even so! The verse oddly calls the ashes 'עָפָר' (dust) — the same word used for the sota's dust, teaching a gezeirah shava.

lines.speaker: Application
lines.text: Just as for the sota, placing the dust first is valid after the fact (בְּדִיעֲבַד), so too here.

lines.speaker: Our mishna's tanna
lines.text: Reads the verse's final clause — 'running water in a vessel' — as specifying that the water must go in first; the earlier clause about ash 'placed on it' just means mixing thoroughly afterward.

callout.label: General principle invoked:
callout.text: 'We find everywhere that the facilitating item goes on top' — supporting the requirement that water precede ash.

slides.title: 🔁 Can a Substitute — or an Offspring — Make Its Own Substitute?
slides.subtitle: The mishna's own halakhic contribution to the tractate

boxes.title: The Sages
items: A substitute animal does NOT generate a further substitute — it stays as it is
The offspring of a consecrated animal does NOT become a substitute either
Consecrated status itself can generate a substitute; nothing derivative from it can

boxes.title: Rabbi Yehuda
items: Agrees a substitute cannot make another substitute
But dissents on offspring: the offspring of a consecrated animal DOES render an exchanged animal a substitute
Position echoed in earlier sugyot (daf 10-11) discussing fetal/offspring sanctity

callout.label: Why it fits the pattern:
callout.text: Like teruma-that-fell-twice or drawn water beyond its threshold, a substitute (or an offspring) is one step removed from the original act of consecration — and the Sages hold that removal caps its generative power.

summary.principle: A whole family of halakhot share one structure — teruma, leaven, drawn water, purification water, a beit haperas, and (per the Sages) a substitute or offspring — none of them propagate their status at full strength into whatever comes next.

flowSteps.content: 🌾 Mishna lists six halakhot where a derivative status is capped or requires calculation
⚖️ Teruma-falls-twice: Rabbis (proportional) vs. R' Eliezer (full strength) — mishna follows the Rabbis

columns.content: 💧 Drawn water: threshold measured by number of vessels (Yosef ben Ḥoni)
🌫️ Mei chatat: water must precede ash, per the majority view

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: a substitute or an offspring is one step removed from consecration — it cannot itself generate a further substitute (R' Yehuda dissents only on offspring)

quiz.q: In the case of a se'ah of teruma-mixture that falls into a second batch of non-sacred produce, what do the Rabbis (followed by our mishna) rule?
o: It renders the second batch forbidden as full teruma
It renders the second batch forbidden only according to the calculated proportion of real teruma present
It has no effect on the second batch at all
It only applies to dough, not produce
quiz.e: The Rabbis hold that once teruma has already been diluted into a mixture, any further transfer carries forward only its proportional (calculated) strength, not the strength of pure teruma — this is the position our mishna follows, against Rabbi Eliezer.

quiz.q: According to Rabba's resolution (via Yosef ben Ḥoni), what determines whether drawn water invalidates a ritual bath?
o: The total volume of drawn water alone
The number of vessels used to pour the drawn water in — 2-3 vessels invalidate it, but 4-5 vessels do not
Whether the water is warm or cold
It is never invalidated by drawn water
quiz.e: Rabba explains the mishna's 'calculation' refers to counting vessels: three log of drawn water poured from two or three vessels invalidates the mikveh, but the same amount spread across four or five vessels does not, per Yosef ben Ḥoni.

quiz.q: What textual technique does Rabbi Shimon use to argue that placing the red heifer's ashes into the vessel before the water is valid after the fact?
o: A kal vachomer from oaths
A gezeirah shava linking the word 'dust' (עָפָר) used for the ashes to the same word used for the sota's dust
He simply overrules the verse
He cites a different verse about teruma
quiz.e: Rabbi Shimon notes the verse calls the ashes 'dust' rather than the more accurate 'ashes,' deriving a verbal analogy to the sota's dust, where placing the dust first is valid after the fact.

quiz.q: According to the Sages in the mishna, can a substitute (temurah) animal itself generate a further substitute?
o: Yes, without limit
No — a substitute does not itself generate another substitute
Only if it is unblemished
Only on Yom Kippur
quiz.e: The mishna states plainly: אֵין תְּמוּרָה עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה — a substitute animal does not generate a further substitute; its status does not propagate further.

quiz.q: What is Rabbi Yehuda's point of disagreement with the Sages regarding the offspring of a consecrated animal?
o: He agrees entirely with the Sages
He holds that the offspring of a consecrated animal DOES render an exchanged animal a valid substitute, unlike the Sages' view
He holds that no animal can ever be consecrated
He disputes only the case of a substitute animal, not offspring
quiz.e: While the Sages hold that neither a substitute nor an offspring can generate a further substitute, Rabbi Yehuda specifically maintains that the offspring of a consecrated animal CAN render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute.
